**The research run stopped before any analysis because the position-protection check failed.** It traded nothing, registered no WATCH plans and changed nothing.

- **What started it:** the automatic shock trigger at 02:05 (GMT+7) / 19:05Z, after unusually large moves in USDCAD (+0.81%), GBPUSD (−0.75%) and the dollar index (+0.73%). That trigger took the place of the missed 12:00 daily slot, so the run went ahead.
- **Why it stopped:** before research starts, a read-only check confirms that open positions are protected. That check needs about 4–6 seconds; this time it hit its 45-second limit. Protection was never confirmed, and the prompt stops the run in that case. None of the three markets was analysed.
- **What I found afterwards (read only):**
  - Verified: one status read took 94 seconds and reported protection as not healthy and new trades as not allowed.
  - Verified: the most recent protective job run (02:13 / 19:13Z) was cut off by Windows Task Scheduler at its 1-minute limit (code 267014, "terminated").
  - Not verified: whether every protective run since the last good check (16:01Z) has also been cut off.
  - Only 2.4 GB of 31.9 GB memory was free. My guess, not tested, is that memory pressure is slowing the protective job past its 1-minute limit.
- **Other gaps:** the usage-reading tool wasn't available in this session, so quota use is recorded as unknown (this doesn't stop a run). No upcoming market event blocked the run.
